name: Fleet Maintenance Checklist
description: A framework for managing maintenance across a vehicle fleet — preventive schedules, inspections, record keeping and compliance.

items.text: Set PM intervals from each manufacturer's schedule
Adjust intervals for usage, mileage and conditions
Schedule oil and filter changes by mileage or time
Plan tire rotations, alignments and replacements
Schedule fluid checks, flushes and belt and hose service
Track upcoming PM due dates for each vehicle
Require driver pre-trip and post-trip inspections
Inspect tires, brakes, lights and steering regularly
Check fluid levels and look for leaks
Inspect wipers, mirrors and safety equipment
Review and act on driver vehicle inspection reports
Log and prioritize defects for repair
Open a work order for every repair
items.note: Capture parts, labor and the technician on record

items.text: Triage defects by safety and urgency
Use qualified technicians or approved vendors
Track repair costs per vehicle to spot problem units
Verify completed repairs before returning to service
Manage warranty and recall work
Keep a complete maintenance history per vehicle
Use fleet software or a central log for records
Record mileage, service dates and costs
Store inspection reports and work orders
Track parts inventory and usage
Document fuel use and monitor efficiency trends
Track registration, insurance and inspection renewals
Monitor emissions and required certifications
Keep driver qualification and licensing records current
Follow the regulations that apply to your fleet
Maintain records to support audits and inspections
Remove unsafe vehicles from service until repaired
Set a maintenance budget and track spend per vehicle
Review uptime, downtime and breakdown trends
Plan vehicle replacement based on age and cost
Standardize procedures and checklists across the fleet
Train drivers on inspections and reporting
Review supplier and vendor performance periodically

faq.q: What is preventive maintenance for a fleet?
faq.a: Preventive maintenance is scheduled servicing done at set mileage or time intervals to keep vehicles reliable, such as oil changes, tire rotations and inspections. Following each manufacturer's schedule across the fleet prevents costly breakdowns and extends vehicle life.

faq.q: How do I set maintenance intervals?
faq.a: Base intervals on each manufacturer's recommended schedule, then adjust for how the vehicle is used, mileage and operating conditions. Severe-duty use, heavy loads and harsh climates call for shorter intervals, so track usage per vehicle rather than applying one rule to all.

Accurate records prove what was done and when, support warranty and resale value, help diagnose recurring issues and demonstrate compliance during audits or inspections. A central log or fleet software keeps history consistent across every vehicle.

faq.q: How does fleet maintenance support compliance?
faq.a: Regular inspections, documented repairs, driver vehicle inspection reports and tracking of registrations, emissions and required certifications help keep a fleet compliant with the regulations that apply to it. Keeping records current avoids fines and out-of-service vehicles.

faq.q: Can I print this fleet maintenance checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it with your fleet records and track preventive schedules, inspections, documentation and compliance for every vehicle.
